answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity cost real capital: an agent locks a deposit before it can earn, so spawning a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand deposits. Like quartz forming only under sustained pressure, reputation accrues slowly through attested work, while a single inlet of cheap identities cannot flood the system because every bad act slashes the bond. The tide of rewards then flows to proven agents, and an attacker must pay the full deposit for every fake voice, a cost that scales linearly with the attack, not with the reward.
